title: Après Polonnaruwa : déclin ou déplacement des centres ?
purpose: Prevent the mobile-capitals sequence from being narrated as one uninterrupted intellectual collapse by contrasting institutional rupture with relocation and renewed patronage.

analysis.core_question: Does the post-Polonnaruwa movement of capitals amount to a continuous collapse of Buddhist learning, or does the evidence show recurrent relocation and reconstruction of scholarly institutions?
analysis.thesis: The evidence better supports discontinuous recomposition: political centres move and institutions are disrupted, yet monastic patronage and literary production reappear in new centres; Kotte is therefore a high point before the distinct Sitawaka/Portuguese-era rupture rather than part of one long decline.

contrast.label: Continuous decline
contrast.position: Loss of Rajarata and repeated invasions progressively erode the old institutional landscape.
contrast.caveat: This captures real rupture but cannot explain the 1344 Gadaladeniya foundation or Kotte's documented literary density.

contrast.label: Mobile recomposition
contrast.position: Monastic and literary capacity relocates with courts, temples, pirivenas and transregional networks.
contrast.caveat: Recomposition does not imply unchanged capacity, uninterrupted lineages or equal strength in every intermediate kingdom.

mechanisms.name: institutional portability
mechanisms.explanation: Patronage and monastic authority can be rebuilt around new shrines and capitals after territorial rupture.

mechanisms.name: scholarly network reproduction
mechanisms.explanation: Grammar, pirivena education and literary lineages reproduce learned culture through teachers, texts and new centres rather than one fixed capital.

mechanisms.name: Sitawaka rupture
mechanisms.explanation: The museum attributes later literary disruption and loss of Pali/Sanskrit composition to Portuguese-era violence and Sitawaka conditions, but the strongest wording still lacks adequate independent closure.

callbacks.relation: Use Kotte as the falsifier of a simple centuries-long intellectual decline.
Return to Sitawaka as a separate research question rather than projecting its decline backwards into Kotte.

content.takeaway: The useful narrative is not a straight fall from Polonnaruwa to Kandy: institutions repeatedly lose their old centre, then reassemble elsewhere; the timing and severity of each rupture must be tested separately.
